comment.body: Thanks for the follow-up and for confirming that the Windows setting meets your use case. The behavior described here is the intentional distinction discussed in #49386: Awake can keep the system awake while allowing the locked display to follow its timeout. Keep screen on is not a promise to override the lock-screen display policy. The reports here do not demonstrate the display timing out while the session is unlocked, so no additional bug report is needed to explain the observed locked-only behavior.

issue_context.summary: The latest replies acknowledge Awake display-off while locked as deliberate behavior and report a Windows-setting alternative.
initial_investigation: Read the complete current body, every comment and timeline, compared the prior judgment, and read the linked #49386 description.
Retained the established documented display/system distinction; no system power setting, session policy or installed module was changed.
inferences: A future request for an optional different lock-screen policy would be an enhancement discussion, not proof this locked-only report violates the present contract.
known_information: The report selects indefinite Awake plus Keep screen on, then observes the display turning off after locking; no unlocked failure is reported.

The latest November 3 participant links #49386, recognizes the deliberate locked-display behavior, and subsequently reports a Windows-setting alternative worked. This response is not a new unlocked regression.
The previously verified Awake documentation distinguishes system-awake mode from the display-on request while locked; #49386 describes the intentional lock/unlock display-request behavior.
issue_context.analysis: The new discussion supports the established expected-behavior explanation rather than a new code defect. Preserve the locked-versus-unlocked distinction; do not propose bypassing session policy or request another diagnostic package. The participant workaround is not independent validation of a PowerToys fix.
